conviction_note: abs_move 7.5 (the name's median reaction is 5.92 and there is no usable chain; raised because this thin, two-analyst name may have to address 2027 US payer coverage on the call) times p_up 37 gives -1.95. That is smaller than the findings' sum of -3.4 because there is a real chance management does not disclose the CVS Caremark 2027 Vascepa removal on 28 Oct. The stock also trades below net cash (~$15/ADS against a $12 spot), which cushions a fall.
bar: Q3 2026 total net revenue of about $44.0M. Benzinga: $44.0M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AMRN/earnings-forecasts). Earnings Whispers: $44.49M (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/AMRN). Yahoo, 2 analysts: $43.71M, low $41.42M (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMRN/analysis/). These three agree within 2%. The EPS consensus is disputed (-$0.07 against -$0.28), so it is not used. The company gives no revenue guidance; it guides to stable US volumes, positive FY26 cash flow and cash up ~10% YoY at YE26 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897448/000119312526323841/amrn-ex99_1.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest was ~528.4K ADS at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 10.5 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/amrn/short-interest/). Against ~21M ADS outstanding that is ~2.5% of shares. Days to cover is high only because turnover is thin (67K ADS/day), so this is not a crowded short. Days to cover swung between 4.7 and 10.8 over August-September. There is no usable option skew: the ATM spread is 111% of mid, put/call OI is 0.42 and total OI is 874. Run-up: 20d -8.7%, 5d +4.5%; the stock is 37.6% off its 52w high and 6% above its 52w low. The controlling activist Sarissa sold ADSs at ~$14.0 on 24-25 Aug 2026 and holds 6.09% (13D/A, 2026-08-27).

findings.finding: CVS Caremark's own formulary update charts, 'current as of October 1, 2026', remove VASCEPA from its Standard Control and Value formularies effective 2027-01-01, with 'icosapent ethyl, omega-3 acid ethyl esters' as the formulary options. CVS's January 2027 Advanced Control Choice drug list (Aetna) lists only generic icosapent ethyl and omega-3 acid ethyl esters in the omega-3 class, with no VASCEPA. This reverses the July 2025 ACCF update, which added VASCEPA and removed generic IPE. Amarin calls that regained exclusive 'a large national PBM' and the main reason Q2 COGS rose. The same PBM's 2024 exit covered ~25% of US Vascepa scripts and took the stock -6.2% premarket. US revenue is $32.2M of $42.2M Q2 revenue. In July management only promised exclusives 'through the end of 2026'. Amarin has filed no 8-K on this, and no news or analyst item mentions it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The analogous PBM loss, announced on 2024-06-04 (8-K plus CEO exit), took the shares -6.2% premarket per Bloomberg Law (https://news.bloomberglaw.com/health-law-and-business/amarin-shares-slump-as-drug-dropped-from-formulary-ceo-exit-1). The Q4 2025 print, where the outlook was the focus, moved -9.47%; Q3 2025 moved -11.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: The documents sit on employer/state benefit sites (tn.gov, aetna.com), not on the wire. Searches for Amarin + CVS/PBM + 2027 return nothing, and there is no 8-K. If it were priced, it would show as a company or analyst disclosure and a gap-down on a dated day. Instead the stock slid gradually: 20d -8.7%, from ~$13.1 to $11.48 on Oct 20, then back to $12 (+4.5% over 5d). That is consistent at most with partial leakage. The two-analyst consensus of ~$44M/quarter does not model 2027. The Q3 call is the first scheduled place management must address 2027 payer status.
findings.independence: Three documents from the counterparty agree. Value Formulary Jan 2027 also removes VASCEPA* (https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/partnersforhealth/documents/Value_Formulary_JAN_2027.pdf). The 2027 Aetna Advanced Control Choice drug list shows the omega-3 class as icosapent ethyl + omega-3 acid ethyl esters only (https://www.aetna.com/content/dam/aetna/pdfs/aetnacom/individuals-families-health-insurance/document-library/pharmacy/2027_Drug_guide_Advanced_Control_Choice.pdf). The July 2025 ACCF update that added VASCEPA is the baseline being reversed (https://www.ehp.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/07-2025-ACCF-Formulary-Change-Updates.pdf). Management's own hedge, 'maintain our exclusives with key payers through the end of 2026', is on the Q2 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943226). All of these are one fact, filed once. Two things cushion it: cash of ~$15/ADS exceeds the $12 price, and other payers' exclusives are not shown to change.

findings.finding: US Vascepa revenue fell from $35.6M in Q1 2026 to $32.2M in Q2 2026 (-10% QoQ), even though management guided US volumes 'consistent' through FY26 and blamed net pricing pressure. Q2 total revenue of $42.2M already missed the ~$44.6M consensus, and the Q3 bar is again ~$44M. If US revenue holds near $31-33M, Europe supply sales to Recordati ~$5-6M (lumpy), ROW ~$1-3M and royalties ~$3M, total revenue lands ~$41-44M, a slight miss. The partial offset is the CFO's statement that COGS 'should level off from Q3 2026'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed revenue ($42.2M against ~$44.6M) and the stock moved +0.49%. Q1 2026 beat revenue and the stock moved +2.36%. The revenue line has paid little on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The run-rate is public. The only element not visible is the sequential trend applied to a bar that sits above the last print.
findings.independence: Q1 split: US $35.6M (https://finviz.com/news/348635/amarin-reports-2026-first-quarter-financial-results). Consensus from three aggregators, listed in bar. COGS comment from the Q2 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943226). This is my own arithmetic on company numbers, an inference.

findings.finding: Sarissa Capital, the activist that controls Amarin's board, sold ADSs at $14.00-14.08 on 24-25 Aug 2026 (several hundred thousand ADS visible in Exhibit 17) and now holds 6.09% of ordinary shares. Selling by the controlling holder during a Barclays-led 'pathways to enhance shareholder value' review lowers the odds that the Q3 release carries a sale or merger announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on prints. The stock has fallen from ~$14 at the sale to $12.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the filing has been public for two months and the stock has fallen 14% since. Residual value: the market may still carry a strategic-outcome option into the call.
findings.independence: Transactions are in Exhibit 17 of the same filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897448/000089914026000972/sexhibit17b.htm), so this is one document. No 13D/A since, which means less than 1% further change.

findings.finding: Amarin holds a UK High Court approval for share repurchases valid through Q2 2029. Cash and investments are $314.6M (about $15.2 per ADS on ~20.7M ADS-equivalents), the company is debt-free and has had three straight quarters of positive cash flow, against a ~$250M market cap. Barclays is retained to explore shareholder-value pathways. Any capital-return announcement with Q3 would land on a stock trading at ~80% of net cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on prints. The Jan 2026 pre-announcement of positive cash flow ahead of plan moved +16.89%, which shows how the stock treats the cash line.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades below net cash. If the market expected a buyback or tender, it would trade near or above cash. The option is unpriced because nothing signals timing, and Sarissa's selling (finding 3) argues against near-term action. That caveat is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Cash and debt-free status are in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897448/000119312526323841/amrn-ex99_1.htm). Market cap of $252M at $12.04 on Oct 9 per PitchBook (https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/43124-41).

findings.finding: The generic icosapent ethyl NADAC benchmark (120 x 1g capsules, ~$53.63) has stayed in a narrow band from February through July 2026. Generic acquisition pricing is not still collapsing, which limits further net-price pressure on the branded US line in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates this industry price series for this name. Its effect is small and indirect, because Vascepa's net price is set by rebates rather than NADAC.
findings.independence: Proxy only, seen as a search snippet (the page returned 403 on fetch). It leans against the US decline in finding 2 but does not contradict it.

findings.finding: The US Supreme Court ruled 9-0 for Hikma on 2026-06-04, reversing the Federal Circuit and ending Amarin's skinny-label induced-infringement claim. Any damages upside is gone and will not appear in the Q3 results.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: public for five months. Filed so the judges can see the litigation option is closed.
